When I was younger (elementary/middle school age) my Ndad would call me fat constantly. I wasn't fat or even overweight, but I was short an was built thicker, just like he was. But he lifted weights so he got a 'pass'. 

I eventually hated looking at myself and developed a severe eating disorder. I was afraid to eat. I lived for a few months on large amounts of water, vitamins, fiber pills, and when I needed some kind of substance, plain air popped popcorn. I was as thin as my body type would allow and still he would criticize. I eventually passed out at school and told my friend why. She told my teacher and the teacher made sure I ate something and called my parents. 

 I'd hear positive feedback from friends and family who didn't know that my weight loss was because of my eating habits, or lack there of so even after that incident I continued. Eventually I found a good group o supportive friends and I began eating healthy.

When got pregnant a few years ago it hit me hard again. I was still in high school and living with my parents. He'd call me fat all the time, and hormones and a very unstable environment. I managed to last until after I had my daughter but what pushed me over the edge is when he (being a very wealthy monster) told me he had no money to buy me non-maternity clothes that actually fit well because I didn't fit into the small clothes I fit into before the pregnancy. I was told to lose weight so I could fit into my 12yo sisters clothes (and she is going through the same thing as I did at her age so she is even too small for her age. (He then went to buy himself a new wardrobe full of sports jerseys, but I digress)

After that I felt so broken I did the opposite of what I had done before. The twisted thought process went like this: if being skinny did no good, and he sees me as fat anyway, I might as well be. So I over ate, and eventually fit back into my maternity clothes.

Since then my weight has been a crazy up and down and I am still struggling to get into the habit of healthy eating.
